commands.command: Decision 0050: bounded repository graph query, orientation, and pagination contract
commands.summary: Defines query authority (read-only, no filesystem crawling/graph mutation/durable writes/provider calls), typed target resolution (exact/ambiguous/not_found, never a fuzzy guess), deterministic traversal, one reusable QueryBounds type with centralized defaults, opaque cursor/pagination binding (contract version + graph fingerprint + operation + normalized request hash + position), byte-budget-authoritative output limits with a documented token estimate, durable-vs-overlay freshness/coverage policy (fail closed on unsupported/corrupt, disclosed stale-by-default with an allow_stale escape hatch that still always discloses freshness=stale), fact-vs-navigation-hint separation, and the legacy generic `graph` engine operation's classification as a frozen, unextended, zero-caller compatibility surface (option A).

199/199 (147 pre-existing at this checkpoint's start + 52 new: 50 query-kernel integration tests, 1 no-source-read-after-load proof, 1 latency-evidence test; plus the 8 cursor/selector unit tests already counted in the 199 total).
Full workspace green: repopact-graph 199, repopact-desktop-api 17 (14 pre-existing + 3 new graph_query tests), repopact-protocol/repopact-engine build and check clean, all others unaffected.
Clean.

GraphQueryEngine<'a> over &'a RepositoryGraph plus a disposable in-memory BTreeMap-based GraphQueryIndex (node/edge adjacency, nodes-by-source-path, nodes-by-role, nodes-by-kind), rebuilt fresh per call, never persisted, never rog/-adjacent. Typed NodeSelector (NodeId/RepositoryPath/WorkItemId/Package/Module/Symbol) resolves to Exact/Ambiguous/NotFound -- never a silent first-match guess; RepositoryPath rejects absolute-host-paths and '..' escapes as malformed input. Operations: resolve, neighbors, path (deterministic bounded BFS distinguishing no_path from search_truncated_before_proof), dependencies (direct/depth-bounded transitive), dependents (normalizing persisted ReverseDependency and query-derived DependsOn-inverse into one shape with disclosed provenance), context, tests (always discloses the ROG-019 fixture-topology gap), governance, impact (impact_semantics=structural_only, never behavioral proof), and orient (composes the above into identity/containment/deps/dependents/tests/surfaces/governance plus a separately-typed, deterministically rank-ordered navigation_hints list -- never mixed with facts, never model-scored).

Opaque base64url-encoded cursor (implemented without a new external dependency) binding query_contract_version + graph fingerprint + operation + SHA-256 of the normalized request + a continuation position. Rejected for a different fingerprint/operation/target/filter set, malformed content, or oversized length. Pagination reconstructs the deterministic bounded result with no duplicates or gaps (proven by a dedicated multi-page test). Hard bounds (max_nodes/max_edges/max_depth/page_size) proven to trigger and truncate rather than silently drop content.

Absent -> typed error with build guidance. Unsupported/corrupt -> fail closed. Stale -> refused by default (typed error), openable with allow_stale, but the returned status.durable_freshness still always reports stale -- proven by a dedicated test that mutates source after a build and confirms both behaviors.

The identical query kernel runs against SessionGraphState::effective_graph(); a dedicated desktop-api test resolves a file added after the session opened (before any durable graph existed) and confirms basis=working_overlay is disclosed and rog/ is never written.

graph.resolve/context/neighbors/path/dependencies/dependents/tests/governance/impact/orient registered in engine dispatch and protocol capabilities(). Each is a thin params-parse-then-delegate adapter (query_ops.rs) -- no traversal logic duplicated. Smoke-tested against RepoPact's own live repository via the raw stdio protocol.

Confirmed exactly what it does (RepoPactCore::graph_snapshot -> an unbounded fresh RepositoryGraph::build every call, no freshness/coverage envelope) and that it has zero callers in this codebase (not Python, not desktop-api). Classified as a legacy pre-ROG compatibility surface (option A): left unmodified, explicitly excluded from the new typed query contract, not wired into any new client.

Explicit mutually-exclusive typed target flags (--id/--path/--work-item/--package/--module/--symbol[+--symbol-path]) map into the engine's NodeSelector; commands other than resolve/orient first call graph.resolve client-side and print an honest ambiguous/not-found result rather than guessing. 8 new pytest tests exercise the real CLI end-to-end.

GraphQueryRequest mirrors the engine protocol's per-operation params; runs the same GraphQueryEngine against SessionGraphState::effective_graph(). No Tauri command wiring, no repository-map UI (ROG-027 untouched) -- backend plumbing only, per this checkpoint's explicit scope.

NodeSelector/SymbolSelector, QueryBounds, FactRef/RelationFact, ResolutionOutcome, every per-operation result type, NavigationHint/HintReason, generic QueryEnvelope<T>, and GraphQueryRequest added to the hand-maintained generate-types.rs template; types.ts regenerated. `tsc --noEmit` and the full vitest suite (16/16) pass. Disclosed, not fixed: GraphNode/GraphEdge TS interfaces were already stale before this checkpoint (missing several current Rust fields) -- out of this checkpoint's scope.
A CountingGitRunner-backed test proves 8 different query operations issue zero additional Git invocations beyond the graph's own construction.

Source files (including Cargo.toml) deleted after graph.build; resolve/orient against the loaded durable graph (with allow_stale, since the freshness recompute correctly detects the deletion) still succeed purely from the in-memory graph.

GraphQueryEngine borrows &RepositoryGraph, never &mut -- no method it exposes can mutate the graph by construction. A dedicated test runs orient/dependencies and asserts the graph is byte-identical (PartialEq) before and after. A separate desktop-api test proves graph_query requires an open session (no ambient graph access).

A 7-file fixture (a 3-item governance dependency chain, a Cargo crate with [[bin]]+[[test]]), hash-verified byte-identical, was built independently via the raw engine stdio protocol on native Windows and a freshly re-synced Linux-native WSL2 Debian checkout (~/repopact-linux, synced via a git bundle of this checkpoint's exact commit, never /mnt/c/...). graph.build/resolve/dependencies/path/orient all produced byte-identical output (fingerprint and every response body, confirmed after normalizing a CRLF/LF artifact introduced by shell redirection on Windows) between platforms. No macOS execution occurred or is claimed.

Against RepoPact's own live repository (8,491 nodes): graph.orient(work_item_id=063) resolved exactly, returning 3 real direct dependencies (054/056/058), 0 direct dependents, 0 relevant tests (honest -- WI063 is a work item, not a test-bearing package), the disclosed fixture-coverage warning, and 16 deterministically rank-ordered navigation hints (21,607 bytes). graph.orient(repository_path=rust/crates/repopact-graph/src/lib.rs) and graph.orient(package=repopact-graph) (11 real package_surfaces, 11,812 bytes) both resolved exactly. graph.resolve(symbol=SessionGraphState) resolved to the unique real symbol node. graph.resolve(package=repopact-desktop) genuinely returned Ambiguous between the real npm package.json and the real Cargo src-tauri crate that both happen to be named 'repopact-desktop' -- a real, previously-unknown naming collision this checkpoint's resolver correctly disclosed rather than silently picking one.

commands.command: Query latency evidence (engineering validation only, not ROG-032 closeout)
commands.summary: On a synthetic fixture: cold graph-open (durable load + freshness projection walk) ~55ms, query-index build ~0.4ms, warm resolve/dependencies/dependents/tests/governance all under 150us, orient (composing several sub-queries) ~340us -- the query kernel itself is fast; almost all latency in a real-repo round trip (~3.1s observed against RepoPact's own ~800-file repository) comes from the pre-existing freshness-check full source-projection walk, not the query kernel. Cold and warm timings are reported separately, never combined into one misleading number.

Dashboard regenerated and committed (this checkpoint's own work-item.json/decision/evidence changes were the only cause of staleness this checkpoint introduced); canonical repopact validate reports only two pre-existing, unrelated diagnostics (see closeout.pre_existing_unrelated_conditions).
20/20 pass (via REPOPACT_ENGINE pointed at the freshly built debug binary), including 8 new query-command tests.
See closeout.python_regression for the exact count captured after this evidence record was finalized.

environment.linux: WSL2 Debian 13 (trixie), Linux-native checkout at ~/repopact-linux (never /mnt/c/...), synced to this checkpoint's exact commit via a git bundle

closeout.decision_0050: accepted -- read-only query authority, typed resolution, deterministic traversal, shared bounds, opaque cursor/pagination, byte-budget-authoritative output limits, durable-vs-overlay freshness/coverage policy, fact-vs-navigation-hint separation, and the legacy `graph` operation's frozen classification are all recorded and implemented exactly as decided
closeout.query_contract_version: 1 (repopact_graph::query::QUERY_CONTRACT_VERSION), independent of graph_schema_version (unchanged at 3) -- no durable schema bump was required or made this checkpoint
closeout.query_kernel_architecture: one canonical repopact_graph::query module (GraphQueryEngine + a disposable in-memory index) reused identically by the engine binary (query_ops.rs), the CLI (through the engine), and the desktop API (DesktopSession::graph_query against SessionGraphState::effective_graph()) -- no traversal logic duplicated in any adapter layer
closeout.target_selectors: NodeId, RepositoryPath (validated, rejects absolute/`..`), WorkItemId, Package (manifest-identity-label match), Module (Symbol with symbol_kind=Module), Symbol (name + optional path/symbol_kind/container disambiguation) -- the AC's 'type' selector clause is satisfied via Symbol{symbol_kind: Some(Type)}, not a seventh selector variant
closeout.legacy_graph_operation: audited and classified as a frozen, zero-caller, pre-ROG compatibility surface (Decision 0050 section 12, option A) -- left exactly as-is, not extended, not wired into any new consumer
closeout.fixture_coverage_disclosure: graph.tests and graph.impact always disclose the fixture-topology warning named by this checkpoint's own ROG-019 instruction; graph.orient includes it whenever the resolved target's neighborhood could plausibly include fixtures. No fixture node or role was fabricated to manufacture ROG-019 satisfaction
closeout.cross_platform_result: a 7-file fixture (governance dependency chain + a Cargo crate with explicit [[bin]]/[[test]]), hash-verified byte-identical source, produces byte-identical build/resolve/dependencies/path/orient output on native Windows and Linux-native WSL2 Debian 13
closeout.real_repopact_evidence: graph.orient against WI063 (3 real dependencies, 16 rank-ordered hints, 21,607 bytes), against rust/crates/repopact-graph/src/lib.rs, and against the repopact-graph package (11 real package_surfaces) all resolved exactly; graph.resolve(symbol=SessionGraphState) resolved uniquely; graph.resolve(package=repopact-desktop) genuinely disclosed Ambiguous between a real npm package.json and a real Cargo crate sharing the name 'repopact-desktop' -- proving the resolver's never-guess contract against a real, previously-unknown naming collision
closeout.query_latency_evidence: cold graph-open ~55ms (dominated by the pre-existing freshness projection walk, not the query kernel), index build ~0.4ms, warm per-operation queries under 150us (orient ~340us) on a synthetic fixture; a real-repo round trip is ~3.1s, attributable almost entirely to the freshness check, not this checkpoint's query kernel -- reported separately, never combined into one misleading number. Engineering evidence only, not ROG-032 closeout
